notes: THE MOST INFORMATIVE ABSENCE ROW IN THIS BUNDLE. This is a mechanistically explained species negative, not a failed experiment: the three rabbit factor IX residues that contact the aptamer (Lys132, Leu162, Arg233 in human) are substituted by Asn, Phe and Trp respectively, as shown by the sequence alignment in Fig. 3F. The source states the contact residues are otherwise conserved across all 101 known mammalian factor IX sequences. A reconstitution control rules out trivial explanations - see the separate hemophilia-B mixing row. Any species-extrapolation model built from this bundle must carry this row, or it will wrongly assume aptamer anticoagulants are species-general.

system_model: 13-week repeat-dose general toxicology study (rat)
timepoint: NOT_REPORTED - label says the effect was 'transient' but gives no sampling times
n_subjects: NOT_REPORTED - group sizes not given in the label
control_description: Concurrent control group implied by a GLP repeat-dose toxicology design but neither described nor quantified in the label
effect_vs_control: Qualitative only: 'transiently prolonged' (APTT) / 'transiently increased' (PT). No magnitudes, no group means, no fold-change, no NOAEL are printed. The label states the doses were 'at least 6 times higher on a mg/m2 basis than the clinical dose of 25 mg/kg/day'.
severity_stated_by_source: transiently prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT)
source_locus: Section 13.2 Animal Toxicology and/or Pharmacology
verbatim_quote: In the 13-week toxicity studies in rats and dogs, intravenous administration of defibrotide sodium transiently prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) at 1200 and 4800 mg/kg/day administered as a continuous infusion in rats and at 300 and 1600 mg/kg/day administered in 2-hour infusions 4 times daily in dogs. Prothrombin time (PT) was also transiently increased at 4800 mg/kg/day in rats. These findings were observed at doses at least 6 times higher on a mg/m2 basis than the clinical dose of 25 mg/kg/day. The effects on APTT and PT may be due to direct effects on coagulation based on the dose-dependent response observed.
notes: Dose-resolved but value-free: the label names the dose levels at which the change occurred and never prints a clotting time. readout_value is NOT_REPORTED and readout_is_qualitative is true accordingly - no number was invented. Both flags true: coagulation modulation is on-target pharmacology for defibrotide, and this is simultaneously a toxicology finding at supratherapeutic exposure. The label supplies the causal attribution itself: 'The effects on APTT and PT may be due to direct effects on coagulation based on the dose-dependent response observed.' Note the label reports the clinical comparator as 25 mg/kg/day, which is the 6.25 mg/kg q6h regimen of Section 2.1 expressed as a daily total. The 4800 mg/kg/day rat level appears in both an aPTT row and the PT row - one dose, two readouts, not a duplicate.

verbatim_quote: The mechanism of action of defibrotide sodium has not been fully elucidated. In vitro, defibrotide sodium enhances the enzymatic activity of plasmin to hydrolyze fibrin clots. Studies evaluating the pharmacological effects of defibrotide sodium on endothelial cells (ECs) were conducted primarily in the human microvascular endothelial cell line. In vitro, defibrotide sodium increased tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) and thrombomodulin expression, and decreased von Willebrand factor (vWF) and plasminogen activator inhibitor‑1 (PAI-1) expression, thereby reducing EC activation and increasing EC‑mediated fibrinolysis.
notes: Qualitative mechanistic row: direction is stated by the label, magnitude is not. Included because fibrinolysis markers (t-PA, PAI-1, plasmin) and vWF/thrombomodulin are coagulation-cascade readouts within this endpoint's scope. vWF and thrombomodulin are reported as EXPRESSION in endothelial cells, not as plasma factor activity - do not treat them as factor-activity assays.

verbatim_quote: Plasma concentrations of PAI-1 were assessed on an exploratory basis as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for efficacy in Study 2. There were no statistically significant differences in mean PAI-1 levels by treatment or outcome.

verbatim_quote: TEAESIs of “any suspected or confirmed thromboembolic events” were reported in 4 (1.4%) participants with AT-DR, corresponding to an EAIR of 0.82 per 100 patient-years ( Table 3 ). None of these events were associated with AT levels of <15% (range, 15.5%-65.3%). Two arterial events (embolic stroke and incidental finding of cerebral infarction) and 2 postoperative venous events (venous thrombosis and DVT) occurred in 1 (0.3%) participant each. Three events were deemed unrelated to fitusiran treatment by the investigator. All 4 participants with thrombotic events had predisposing clinical risk factors; furthermore, doses and frequency of CFC/BPA administered exceeded BMGs in both postoperative venous events ( Table 4 ).

Crucially, none of the four occurred at AT <15% (range 15.5%-65.3%), so residual thrombotic risk on the AT-based regimen is not explained by pharmacodynamic overshoot alone. Three of four were judged unrelated by the investigator; both post-operative venous events involved CFC/BPA dosing above the bleed management guidelines.

source_locus: Results, Assessment of AT activity levels and TG
verbatim_quote: Consistent with the mechanism of action of fitusiran, TG increased with AT lowering ( Figure 2 B; supplemental Figure 7 ), from a mean at baseline of 17 nM (SD, 10) to a peak mean of 74 nM (SD, 27) by end point evaluation (ie, last available assessment under the original dose regimen) that remained elevated during the course of fitusiran treatment for the overall participants in the original dose regimen period (ie, 66 months). In the AT-based dose regimen period, TG increased from a mean at baseline of 15 nM (SD, 6) to a peak mean of 88 nM (SD, 29) by end point evaluation (ie, last available assessment on AT-based dose regimen) for the overall participants, although TG assessments were only included for the first 6 months under the AT-based dose regimen.
notes: ON-TARGET. MAJOR CAVEAT stated by the source: a new batch of thrombin-generation trigger reagent introduced on 06 October 2021 corrupted the assay, so samples from 17 of the 18 AT-based-dose-regimen participants were excluded and only the first 6 months of AT-DR thrombin generation data are included. The 88 nM figure therefore rests on a very small sample. Per-participant trajectories are only in Figure 2B (a spaghetti plot) and were not read.

verbatim_quote: The participant with CVA was a 37-year-old male with a history of right lower extremity deep vein thrombosis not known by the investigator at the time of enrollment (exclusion criterion), and several risk factors including diabetes and possible hypertension and hyperlipidemia around the time of the event. This participant experienced complete left-sided weakness and then likely developed right middle cerebral artery territory infarct hemorrhagic with transformation and subsequent subarachnoid bleed. On 2 consecutive days before the CVA onset, the participant was treated with recombinant FVIII for a spontaneous bleed. The AT values range before the event onset was 9% to 13%. The participant recovered from the event with sequelae 28 days after the onset. The CVA was classified by the investigator as serious and possibly related to fitusiran, resulting in fitusiran discontinuation and study withdrawal.
notes: readout_value is the pre-event AT activity range, not an event count. AT was in the 9%-13% band, i.e. below the 15% floor later adopted as the safety threshold. Confounders acknowledged by the source: undisclosed prior deep vein thrombosis (an exclusion criterion), diabetes, possible hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and recombinant FVIII on the 2 preceding days.

source_locus: Results, Safety (AESI narrative for the thrombosis on papilla)
verbatim_quote: The participant with thrombosis was a 56-year-old male, with papilledema of both eyes 10 days before the event onset. He experienced pain in eye with the thrombosis onset. No bleeds were reported immediately before the thrombosis, and the participant did not use CFCs or BPAs. It was suspected that there was obstruction in the capillary vessels in the eyes. The investigator considered it possible that the observed papilledema was secondary to a thrombotic event in a capillary that supplies the optic nerve. A brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed inflammatory changes in the maxillary sinus and normal orbital structures; magnetic resonance venography was unremarkable. The AT values range before the thrombosis onset was 9% to 11%. The thrombosis on papilla was classified as nonserious and assessed by the investigator as possibly related to fitusiran.
notes: Cleanest fitusiran-attributable thrombotic case in this bundle: no concomitant factor concentrate or bypassing agent was used, so the additive-procoagulant confounder present in most other cases is absent. Occurred during follow-up, 87 days after the last dose, while AT was still suppressed.

verbatim_quote: In part D, the mean (standard error of the mean [SEM]) baseline AT activity was 109.5% (4.4) and 100.2% (4.8) in the fitusiran 50 mg and 80 mg dose groups, respectively. Because baseline levels may vary between individuals, we evaluated AT reduction based on percentage of AT activity relative to individual participant baseline. There was consistent reduction in AT activity with fitusiran treatment, evident initially at day 7 and progressing to maximal effect after day 28. The mean nadir AT activity was similar between the two dose groups, specifically, 18.0% in the 50 mg dose group and 12.6% in the 80 mg dose group, corresponding to an 82.0% and 87.4% reduction from baseline, respectively. The minimum residual postdose AT level was 9.8%, observed in the 80 mg dose group.
notes: ON-TARGET DOSE-RESPONSE ANCHOR: this is the magnitude of antithrombin lowering per dose that makes the later thrombotic events interpretable as overshoot of the same axis. The minimum residual post-dose AT level anywhere in the study was 9.8% (80 mg group), i.e. inside the <10% stratum later linked to the highest thrombotic incident rate.

verbatim_quote: FIGS. 24A-D show the relationship between relative serum Serpinc1 level and fold change in peak plasma thrombin level at a single A) 1 mg/kg, B) 3 mg/kg, C) 10 mg/kg, and D) 30 mg/kg dose of compound AD57213. Serpinc1 levels are represented relative to the average of three pre-dose measurements. Thrombin generation curves were generated from plasma samples collected at various time points using a Calibrated Automated Thrombinoscope (tissue factor=1 pM). delivery_method: subcutaneous injection twice a week for three weeks
dose_unit: mg/kg per dose (twice weekly for 3 weeks)

effect_vs_control: Thrombus formation (30 μm in diameter) occurred in mice treated with ISIS 404071 at 14.8±1.7 minutes. system_model: Patients undergoing elective primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty; phase 2 open-label randomised parallel-group adaptive trial NCT01713361 (FXI-ASO TKA), 19 centres in 5 countries
timepoint: All events during study treatment and follow-up until day 136 (safety population)
exposure_duration: 36 days pre-operative dosing plus post-operative doses; follow-up to day 136
control_description: Enoxaparin 40 mg once-daily comparator arm, N = 72 (there is no placebo arm in this trial)
effect_vs_control: Arm: FXI-ASO 200 mg. Risk difference vs enoxaparin for the principal safety outcome was −6 (−12 to 1) for 200 mg and −6 (−13 to 2) for 300 mg; Fisher exact P = 0.09 and 0.16 respectively - i.e. numerically LESS bleeding on the ASO, not significantly so.
severity_stated_by_source: The rate of major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was lower with the 300-mg dose regimen than with enoxaparin (3% vs 8%), a difference that did not reach statistical significance.

verbatim_quote: Principal safety outcome: major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding — no. (% [95% CI]) | 4 (3 [1 to 7]) | 2 (3 [<1 to 9]) | 6 (8 [3 to 17])
notes: Table row rendered cell-by-cell in printed column order: FXI-ASO 200 mg (N=144) | FXI-ASO 300 mg (N=77) | enoxaparin 40 mg (N=72). The em dash and the footnote marker are the source's. system_model: Healthy volunteers in three phase I studies (first-in-human/Caucasian, Japanese, Chinese), pooled as the interethnic pharmacodynamic analysis set (iPDS)
timepoint: Emax - maximum ratio to baseline after a single injection; the maximum was mainly observed between Day 15 and Day 30
exposure_duration: single dose, followed for up to 149 days
control_description: Same group's own baseline aPTT in seconds (Table 1, geometric mean/CV%(min-max)); the matched placebo groups showed no aPTT effect at all
effect_vs_control: Ethnicity: Caucasian. Dose-ordered within each ethnicity (40 < 80 ~ 120). Interethnic ANCOVA point estimates for Chinese/Japanese vs Caucasian were 'close to 1'.
severity_stated_by_source: Fesomersen demonstrated good safety and tolerability in all three studies. No major bleeding events were observed.
source_locus: Results, section 'PD', third paragraph (aPTT); values also plotted in Figure 3
verbatim_quote: Geometric mean (CV, %) of the maximum ratios to baseline of aPTT in Caucasian, Japanese, and Chinese participants with fesomersen 40 mg were 1.221 (4.8), 1.188 (7.7), and 1.121 (8.7), respectively; with fesomersen 80 mg were 1.414 (3.3), 1.324 (12.1), and 1.241 (8.7), respectively; and with fesomersen 120 mg were 1.397 (5.1), 1.369 (21.0), and 1.308 (13.5), respectively.
notes: Geometric mean with geometric CV% in parentheses, expressed as a RATIO to that participant's own baseline - not seconds. Value assigned by position in the printed sentence (order: Caucasian, Japanese, Chinese; then 40, 80, 120 mg). Note the 80 mg Caucasian ratio (1.414) exceeds the 120 mg Caucasian ratio (1.397), so the dose-response is not strictly monotonic at the top of the range in the small Caucasian cohorts (n=4 each).

system_model: Healthy volunteers in three phase I studies (first-in-human/Caucasian, Japanese, Chinese), pooled as the interethnic pharmacodynamic analysis set (iPDS)
timepoint: Emax - minimum ratio to baseline after a single injection; maximum inhibition mainly between Day 15 and Day 30
exposure_duration: single dose, followed for up to 149 days
control_description: Same group's own baseline FXI activity in U/mL (Table 1); 'Injection of placebo had no effect on FXI activity (Figure 2).'
effect_vs_control: Ethnicity: Caucasian. Dose-dependent fall: at 120 mg FXI activity reaches 0.26-0.36 of baseline. This is the on-target axis that the aPTT row must be read against.
source_locus: Results, section 'PD', first paragraph (FXI activity); values also plotted in Figure 2
verbatim_quote: Geometric mean (CV, %) of the minimum ratios to baseline of FXI activity in Caucasian, Japanese, and Chinese participants with fesomersen 40 mg were 0.596 (12.9), 0.480 (35.2), and 0.570 (27.3), respectively; with fesomersen 80 mg were 0.381 (41.4), 0.369 (21.6), and 0.362 (28.2), respectively; and with fesomersen 120 mg were 0.260 (21.1), 0.360 (71.7), and 0.268 (73.5), respectively.
notes: Geometric mean with geometric CV% in parentheses; a RATIO to the participant's own baseline. Value assigned by position in the printed sentence. THE ATTRIBUTION POINT: because the aPTT rise and the FXI fall are measured in the same participants at the same visits and correlate ('aPTT increased with decreasing FXI activity in a consistent manner as illustrated by the scatterplot (Figure 4)'), the aPTT prolongation here is on-target FXI depletion, not the transient concentration-driven 2'MOE class effect described in S18. The class effect peaks 4-8 h post-dose and is gone by 24 h, whereas this effect peaks at Day 15-30. The 120 mg Japanese and Chinese CVs are enormous (71.7% and 73.5%).

The 4-8 h peak with return to baseline by 24 h is the diagnostic signature: any contact-pathway aPTT row in this dataset whose peak sits at that time scale should be flagged as class effect rather than target engagement. The '∼' is the source's own U+223C approximately sign.

The aPTT assay is SATURATED by PS content at 2 mg/mL in vitro, so it has no dynamic range left to separate a toxic sequence from a safe one. effect_direction is deliberately NOT_REPORTED, never no_change. verbatim_quote: Measurement of the drugs and monomeric aptamers at molecular equivalence (0.33 μM) in human plasma using the aPTT assay demonstrated a relative aPTT of M08s-1 at 20 s, which was the longest of those tested and was greater than that of previously reported aptamers and even of drugs (Figure 2B). This tendency was also observed in mouse plasma (Figure 2C), suggesting that M08s-1 at a monomer level was the most potent thrombin inhibitor among the tested aptamers and drugs.
notes: MATCHED-DOSE PANEL: every compound in Figure 2B/2C was tested at the same molar concentration (0.33 uM), which is what makes these rows directly comparable across compounds. Control aPTT is carried on every row per the bundle instruction. Readout is RELATIVE aPTT (a difference), defined by the source as: "The “relative aPTT” was calculated by subtracting the aPTT of PBS spiked in human plasma (27 s) from the aPTT of a tested sample spiked in human plasma.". Concentration arithmetic check: methods say 1.6 uL of 30 uM aptamer + 48.4 uL plasma + 50 uL aPTT reagent + 50 uL CaCl2 = 0.32 uM final in 150 uL, consistent with the stated 0.33 uM ("1.6 μL of each pre-annealed 30 μM aptamers in PBS and 48.4 μL of normal human plasma or normal mouse plasma were incubated at 37°C for 1 min using a fully automated blood coagulation instrument (CA-620; Sysmex, Japan). Then, 50 μL of aPTT reagent (Thrombocheck; Sysmex) was added and further incubated at 37°C for 2 min. Then, 50 μL of 0.025 M calcium chloride was added, and aPTT was measured immediately by tracking the change in scattered light intensity over time at 660 nm. The experiments were performed in triplicate."). CONTROL-VALUE CONFLICT: the body text of the same paper gives the human control as "27 s", the Figure 2 caption as 27.1 s, and supplementary Figure S12 as 28.7 s - see extraction_notes hazard #3. Compound identities for this paragraph: "We first investigated the anticoagulant activity of the monomeric M08s-1 and compared this with the known anti-thrombin DNA aptamers TBA13, TBA29, RE31,42 and NU172 (Figures S2A–S2D); in addition, the argatroban and bivalirudin anti-thrombin drugs indicative of HIT were tested (Figures S1A and S1B)." - NOTE the source writes "TBA13" here, while Figure S2a and Table S1 both give TBA15.

system_model: Purified human alpha-thrombin (6.25 nM) plus purified human fibrinogen (6 uM); turbidity at 350 nm read on an Epoch plate reader
delivery_method: Aptamer (12.5 nM) pre-incubated with thrombin 15 min at room temperature, then fibrinogen added
control_description: No-aptamer thrombin + fibrinogen clotting curve; the control clotting time is plotted in Figure 1D/1E but never printed numerically
effect_vs_control: Grouped by the source's own Figure S3b annotation under "No inhibition" (X = 0, 9, 13, or 21 bp).
source_locus: Results, "Design of M08s-1-based bivalent anti-thrombin aptamers" (Figures 1D and 1E); "No inhibition" grouping from supplementary Figure S3b (mmc1.pdf p.4)
verbatim_quote: When the duplex linker was composed of base pairs with homo-dT and homo-dA chains, where the base pair length was variable (X = 0, 5, 9, 13, 17, and 21 bp in Figure 1C), the clotting was nearly completely inhibited by a linker length with 5 and 17 bp, reflecting high anticoagulant activity via thrombin inhibition (Figure 1D).
notes: THROMBIN CLOTTING TIME (TCT) in a PURIFIED fibrinogen system, not plasma - assay defined by the source as: "Screening of the duplex linker was performed based on thrombin clotting time (TCT) with purified fibrinogen, where fibrin cleaved from fibrinogen by thrombin spontaneously aggregates to increase the turbidity of the solution as a result of “clotting”; inhibition of thrombin by the aptamer prolongs the clotting time (Figure 1C)." and run per "Briefly, to a 0.6-mL tube, 100 μL of pre-annealed 12.5 nM aptamer in PBS and 100 μL of 6.25 nM human thrombin in PBS were added and incubated at room temperature for 15 min.". NO NUMBER EXTRACTED: every clotting time in this screen is plotted only in Figure 1D/1E. effect_direction "no_change" for this variant rests on the source's OWN Figure S3b annotation, which prints "X = 5 or 17 bp X = 0, 9, 13, or 21 bp No inhibition"; the body text only says 5 and 17 bp were the active lengths. A reviewer should treat this as the source asserting a null, not as a quantified null. Figure S3 legend: "(b) Possible mechanism for strong inhibition activity of the Pse08- 29 with 5 bp and 17 bp linkers. These would be either 2:2 or 3:3 complex forms and when an inappropriate, rigid linker doesn’t allow two aptamer moieties to simultaneously bind to the same a- Thrombin.". This series is the clean sequence-to-phenotype block of the bundle: 11 near-identical constructs differing only in duplex-linker length and composition, each with a published sequence, showing a non-monotonic 5 bp / 17 bp activity window.

notes: Group mean as printed; the patent prints no SD, SEM, n-per-timepoint or statistical test for Tables 86-88, so 'increase'/'decrease' describes the sign of the difference between the two printed group means only and carries no claim of statistical significance. CONTRADICTION: the prose immediately above these tables asserts that PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered. For aPTT (Table 87) and for fibrinogen (Table 88) in the 420921/420922/420950/420957/420959 groups the printed table values contradict that assertion. The prose claim is preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on every row. PT differences here are small (all within about 1 second of the PBS group) and are the one readout in this example for which the prose null claim looks consistent with the printed numbers; direction is still recorded from the printed values rather than being rounded to no_change, because the patent supplies no variance with which to justify calling it a null. The '0 hr' column is likewise not defined as pre-dose. Note that the 0 hr values already separate the groups (e.g. Table 87, ISIS 420957 29.13 s vs PBS 19.40 s at 0 hr), which is consistent with the time course being run after weeks of repeat dosing rather than after a single first dose.
